title: Calibration artifacts and batching stability study for FP8/INT8 variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: build a repeatable calibration artifact pipeline and run a focused sensitivity study that measures throughput and tail-latency interactions for FP8 and INT8 quantized model variants across batching strategies and long-context scenarios. Scope includes: - defining calibration dataset sampling strategy and config formats; - producing stable per-layer scale/zero-point artifacts for offline PTQ runs; - running throughput/latency suites on representative hardware (H100, A100) with realistic RPC sizes and KV-cache warm/cold states; - measuring accuracy regressions (perplexity, top-1 token accuracy, and a small generation quality set) and mapping trade-offs. Out-of-scope: QAT experiments and full production rollout automation (follow-up tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Calibration pipeline can generate reproducible artifacts (calib-config + per-layer scales) from a 5k/20k token calibration corpus
Benchmark harness runs FP8 and INT8 artifacts with three batching strategies (micro: 1-2, typical: 4-16, bulk: 32-64) and reports p50/p95/p99 latency and aggregate throughput
Accuracy report contains perplexity delta against FP32 baseline and token-level top-1 delta, with actionable thresholds flagged (>=1% token drop or >5% perplexity increase),
Artifacts and configs are checked into internal storage, with links included in ticket and a basic README describing provenance and usage
A short playbook describing when to use cached-prefix optimization vs cache-disabled execution for quantized variants is drafted and approved by runtime owner
milestones: M1: Define calibration config schema and sampling policy (Mar 11)
M2: Implement artifact serializer and storage integration (Mar 13)
M3: Run baseline FP32 vs FP8/INT8 sweep on H100 for 1k/4k contexts (Mar 16)
M4: Produce final report and playbook (Mar 20)
notes: 2026-03-10: Kickoff — agreed to reuse existing redwood-evals prompt sets for generation quality and a 5k-sample calibration corpus drawn from product logs (PII removed).
2026-03-11: Design decision — use per-channel symmetric quantization for activations and per-tensor for weights to reduce calibration noise; recorded rationale in Confluence (link below).

2026-03-12: Early run — FP8 artifacts produced using offline collector; observed 2.2% top-1 token accuracy drop in cold-KV runs at batch size 32. Investigating whether KV cache handling in the runtime causes precision-sensitive branching.

2026-03-13: Trade-off discussion with runtime team — enabling continuous batching improved throughput by ~28% for INT8 but increased p99 latency by 12ms on H100 for long-context scenarios; agreed to include cache-warm and cache-cold splits in reports.
2026-03-14: Added instrumented benchmark harness to capture token-level divergence traces; initial dashboard URL included below.
technical_details: Calibration method: static PTQ using max-abs and KL divergence clipping heuristics; experiment sets include per-layer min/max and 99.9th percentile range
Calibration corpus: redwood-longseq-calib-20k (public-like prompts stripped of PII), sampling stratified by sequence length (<=512, 512-2048, 2048-8192)
Bench hardware: NVIDIA H100 (4x), A100 (8x) testbeds; inference runtime configured with continuous batching and explicit batch windows to simulate PLG traffic patterns
Scenario matrix: context lengths = [512, 2048, 4096, 8192]; batch sizes = [1, 4, 16, 64]; KV-cache states = [cold, warm]; model variants = [FP32 baseline, INT8, FP8-e4m3, FP8-e5m2],
Metrics collected: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency (generation), tail token latency, perplexity on held-out calibration set, token-level top-1 accuracy delta, ROUGE-L on short summarization prompts
Artifact format: YAML header with model-rev, calibration-seed, per-layer scale/list-of-quant-params and checksum; compatibility checks in harness validate shapes before loading
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Calibration overfitting to the calibration corpus causing blindspots on rare tokens — Mitigation: hold out rare-token slices and run targeted verification
Risk: KV-cache numeric divergence between FP32 and quantized runtime due to fused-kernel differences — Mitigation: add cache-consistency mode that forces cache-validated paths for debugging
Risk: Continuous batching masks latency spikes seen in production — Mitigation: include micro-batch-run with strict SLO timing and simulate live small bursts
